title: Incremental Instruction Compiler — design scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratch for an Incremental Instruction Compiler (IIC) concept — compile user instructions into lightweight, cacheable execution primitives for better reuse, deterministic partial evaluation, and cheaper KV/prefix cache hits. Not a full proposal; focusing on API shape, compile stages, runtime invariants and fallback heuristics.

Goals (top-level):
- Turn messy human instructions into a sequence of semantics-first primitives (ops) that the serving runtime can cheaply validate, cache, and route.
- Allow partial reuse across sessions/tenants while preserving privacy boundaries (no leaking user tokens/credentials).
- Support progressive refinement (incremental compilation) so long instructions can be compiled and executed in stages.
- Fast failure & safe fallback to plain-text execution when compilation fails.

Non-goals:
- Not trying to replace model prompt engineering tools. Not an optimizer for generation quality; primarily cost/latency reuse layer.

API shape (sketch):
POST /compile-instruction
payload: {
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "instruction": "string",
  "context_hints": ["short strings"], // optional
  "privacy_level": "redacted|identifier|full",
  "compile_mode": "eager|incremental|validate-only",
  "max_stages": 3
}
response (200): {
  "compile_id": "uuid",
  "stages": [ /* array of stage metadata */ ],
  "ops_digest": "sha256",
  "cacheable": true|false,
  "warnings": ["strings"]
}

Example ops (informal):
- READ_PROMPT(template_id) — fetch static template from tenant store (no user PII)
- INJECT_CONTEXT(kv_anchor) — attach cached anchor (refers to KV cache key)
- SANITIZE(allowlist) — redact disallowed patterns
- SPLIT_CHUNK(sz=512) — canonical chunk boundaries for prefix caching
- RERANK(cands) — runtime calls reranker with small candidate set

Compile stages (flow):
1) Parse & tokenize (fast): identify template-like pieces, explicit tool calls, and placeholders.
2) Normalize (medium): canonicalize dates, numbers, dot-notation paths, low-risk canonicalization.
3) Materialize ops (slow-ish): emit ops, annotate which ops reference tenant state vs ephemeral user state.
4) Validate & sign-off: check for privacy policy violations; if failing -> return validated=false and explain fallback.

Caching model:
- Key = sha256(tenant_id + ops_digest + privacy_tag + canonical_context_signature)
- Cacheability depends on ops being free of ephemeral user secrets and not referencing per-request tokens.
- Partial-stage caching: stages 1..N can be cached independently (e.g., tokenization + normalization cached globally per tenant).
- TTL: default 1h for normalized ops, 24h for template resolution, configurable via tenant policy.

Runtime invariants (must hold):
- Compiled ops are idempotent for the same input and privacy_level.
- Any op that reads tenant secrets must be executed only in a Private deployment or Dedicated with proper KMS access.
- If compiled ops cannot be safely executed, the runtime falls back to "raw-exec" and annotates traces with compile_failure_reason.

Fallback heuristics (extracted from quick thoughts):
- If compile took > 200ms AND cache miss => try incremental mode (stream first-stage ops to runtime, continue compile in background).
- If sanitizer emits >2 high-severity warnings => deny compilation and force raw-exec with masking layer.
- If compile references >1 external resource fetch (templates, tenant graph) and environment==hosted-api => prefer raw-exec unless tenant has allow-list.

Observability hooks (must instrument):
- compile_latency_ms, stages_completed, cache_hit (bool), ops_count, compile_failure_code, privacy_level, tenant_id (pseudonymized).
- Attach sampled ops_digest to trace for debugging (never include user text).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to represent probabilistic ops (e.g., paraphrase->normalize) in a deterministic op set? Need an 'approximation' tag and fallback to re-run model stage.
- Privacy metadata schema needs standardization across runtime + console (privacy_level mapping to KMS access).
- Operator ergonomics: CLI to inspect compiled ops and re-run in local sandbox.
- Granular billing: should compiled-op cache hits be billed at lower token rate? (product ask)

Quick ASCII diagram:
[Client] --(instruction)--> [Compile API] --(ops_digest)--> [Ops Cache]
                                       |-> [Compile Worker] -> [Validation] -> [Signed Ops]
                                       |->(if cache hit) [Runtime Executor] -> Model

Notes-to-self:
- Cross-link to runtime PR above; will prototype compile-only service behind feature flag INF-3421.
- Experiment idea: attach a "replay key" in compiled package so later model tuning/eval can re-run deterministic ops sequence.
- Keep this doc short; move to confluence if experiments show >2x cache hit improvement.

Slack refs: #eng-runtime thread "iic-proto" (search: "iic sketch feb")
GitHub: runtime/pulls/712 (proto stubs)
Jira: INF-3421 (spike + POC)

-- Jordan (brain dump)
